outcomeNote: Mishna ruling with a dissent by R' Yosei HaGelili

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ בַּכֹּל כּוֹתְבִים – בִּדְיוֹ, בְּסַם, בְּסִיקְרָא, וּבְקוֹמוֹס, וּבְקַנְקַנְתּוֹם, וּבְכׇל דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא שֶׁל קַיָּימָא. אֵין כּוֹתְבִין לֹא בְּמַשְׁקִין, וְלֹא בְּמֵי פֵירוֹת, וְלֹא בְּכׇל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִתְקַיֵּים.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «One may write» a bill of divorce «with any» material that can be used for writing: «With deyo, with paint [sam], with sikra, with komos, with kankantom or with anything that» produces «permanent» writing. However, «one may not write with» other «liquids, nor with fruit juice, nor with anything» that does «not» produce «permanent» writing.

segments.he: עַל הַכֹּל כּוֹתְבִין – עַל הֶעָלֶה שֶׁל זַיִת; וְעַל הַקֶּרֶן שֶׁל פָּרָה – וְנוֹתֵן לָהּ אֶת הַפָּרָה; עַל יָד שֶׁל עֶבֶד – וְנוֹתֵן לָהּ אֶת הָעֶבֶד. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר: אֵין כּוֹתְבִין לֹא עַל דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ רוּחַ חַיִּים, וְלֹא עַל הָאוֹכָלִים.
segments.en: Similarly, with regard to the document itself, «one may write on anything,» even «on an olive leaf, or on the horn of a cow. And» the latter is valid if «he gives her the» entire «cow.» Likewise, one may write a bill of divorce «on the hand of a slave, and» that is valid if «he gives her the slave. Rabbi Yosei HaGelili» disagrees and «says: One may not write» a bill of divorce «on any living thing, nor» may it be written «on food.»

moves.summary: Any permanent ink is valid; liquids and fruit juice are not
Any surface, even an olive leaf, cow's horn, slave's hand
Not on living things or food
